title: Anonymized, avatar-based survey of a normal-weight control sample on body image among adolescents, compared with baseline data from the STARKIDS intervention study
summary: Many children and adolescents with overweight are dissatisfied with their bodies and experience devaluation because of their weight. The STARKIDS study has already collected such data from adolescents with overweight or obesity and from parents. However, a normal-weight comparison group is still missing. In this study, normal-weight adolescents aged 12 to 17 years and parents of normal-weight adolescents in this age range complete a one-time online questionnaire of about 10 minutes. At its core is a computer-generated body figure (avatar) that can be adjusted with a slider. Participants use it to indicate how they perceive the adolescent’s current body, desired body and the body ideal expected by society. This makes it possible to compare how adolescents and adults perceive bodies and whether these views differ between normal weight and overweight. In addition, questions on body satisfaction and on weight-related prejudice and teasing are asked. The survey is anonymous. The results are intended to help improve prevention and treatment programmes for children and adolescents.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adolescents aged 12 to 17 years, or a parent or legal guardian of an adolescent aged 12 to 17 years; normal weight of the adolescent according to age- and sex-specific BMI percentiles (Kromeyer-Hauschild; BMI ≥ P10 and < P90); electronic informed consent (for adolescents aged 12 to 15 years, consent of a legal guardian plus the adolescent’s own assent).
Exclusion criteria:
BMI of the adolescent outside the normal-weight range (BMI < P10 or ≥ P90 according to Kromeyer-Hauschild); insufficient ability to independently understand and complete the study information and questionnaires in German.
